traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz's description of the legume family (the DELTA distribution's own page for it, read 2026-10-15): flowers papilionaceous in Papilionoideae, commonly with the two ventral petals joined as the keel; calyx 5, gamosepalous in most Papilionoideae; androecium often 9-10; gynoecium of one carpel (usually), superior. That the stamens are fused in one tube in the genus is the genus's, not this page's. VicFlora and the Flora of New Zealand on Lupinus polyphyllus, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): corolla 12 to 20 mm; calyx 2-lipped.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 483), genus Lupinus: annual to perennial herbs or shrubs 5-240 cm tall; leaves alternate, palmately compound or rarely of one leaflet, stipulate, with usually 5-17 leaflets (rarely 3 or 4); flowers 5-20 mm long, in racemes; calyx two-lipped; stamens 10, all joined, the anthers alternately long and short; pod flattened.
